question:
A 64-year-old man with a history of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection that was unresponsive to prior
treatment with peginterferon, ribavirin, and telaprevir presents for follow-up. He has a history of alcohol
use disorder but has remained sober for the past 3 years. He denies tobacco or recreational drug use.
On physical examination, scattered spider telangiectasias are noted on the anterior chest wall. The
abdomen is nontender, the liver edge is not palpable, and the tip of the spleen is palpable 1 cm below
the costal margin in the right lateral decubitus position. Laboratory results reveal an international
normalized ratio of 1.3, HCV genotype 1a, HCV RNA level of 1,500,000 IU/mL, and negative serologic
findings for hepatitis A, hepatitis B, and HIV. Additional findings are as follows: | | Patient value |
Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | | Alanine aminotransferase (U/liter) | 49 | 0–35 | | Aspartate
aminotransferase (U/liter) | 85 | 0–35 | | Alkaline phosphatase (U/liter) | 70 | 30–120 | | Total bilirubin
(mg/dL) | 1.0 | 0.3–1.0 | | Albumin (g/dL) | 3.0 | 3.5–5.5 | | Leukocyte count (per mm3) | 4000 | 4500 -
11,000 | | Hemoglobin (g/dL) | 10.2 | 13.5 - 17.5 | | Platelet count (per mm3) | 130,000 | 150,000 -
350,000 | Which of the following screening tests is most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices:
(A) CT scan of the abdomen and serum alpha-fetoprotein (B) Liver biopsy and serum alpha-fetoprotein
(C) MRI of the liver and serum alpha-fetoprotein (D) Abdominal ultrasound and liver function tests (E)
Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and measurement of serum alpha-fetoprotein (F) CT scan of the
